# 🦀 Complete Rust Systems Mastery Track

Welcome to your full Rust learning workspace initialized with **Trak**.

## 📚 Comprehensive Module Index

| Module | Title | Key Topics |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `00-setup-and-cargo-toolchain` | **Setup & Toolchain** | `rustup`, `cargo`, `rustc`, toolchain components (`clippy`, `rustfmt`) |
| `01-basics-and-variables` | **Basics & Variables** | Immutability by default, `mut`, `const`, `static`, variable shadowing |
| `02-data-types-and-memory` | **Data Types & Memory** | Primitives, Tuples, Stack-allocated Arrays, scalar types |
| `03-strings-and-slices` | **Strings & Slices** | `String` (Heap) vs `&str` (Fat Pointer), slice references `&[T]` |
| `04-control-flow-pattern-matching` | **Control Flow** | `if` expressions, `loop` with break value, exhaustive `match`, `if let`, `let else` |
| `05-functions-and-closures` | **Functions & Closures** | Pure functions, `Fn`, `FnMut`, `FnOnce`, `move` closures |
| `06-ownership-borrowing-lifetimes` | **Ownership & Lifetimes** | Move semantics, Copy vs Clone, Aliasing XOR Mutability (`&` vs `&mut`), Lifetimes `'a` |
| `07-structs-enums-methods` | **Structs & Enums** | Named structs, tuple structs, unit structs, enum payloads, `impl` blocks |
| `08-traits-and-generics` | **Traits & Generics** | Trait definitions, trait bounds, Static (`impl Trait`) vs Dynamic dispatch (`dyn Trait`) |
| `09-collections-and-iterators` | **Collections & Iterators** | `Vec<T>`, `HashMap<K, V>`, `BTreeMap`, lazy iterators: `map`, `filter`, `fold` |
| `10-error-handling-custom-errors` | **Error Architecture** | `Option<T>`, `Result<T, E>`, `?` carrier operator, custom error enums |
| `11-smart-pointers-interior-mutability` | **Smart Pointers** | `Box<T>`, `Rc<T>`, `Arc<T>`, `RefCell<T>`, `Mutex<T>`, interior mutability |
| `12-modules-packages-imports` | **Modules & Crates** | Modern 2018+ module tree, `pub(crate)`, re-exports `pub use` |
| `13-attributes-and-serde` | **Attributes & Serde** | Derive macros, JSON serialization/deserialization with `serde` |
| `14-async-rust-and-tokio` | **Async & Tokio** | `async`/`await`, `Future` trait, `tokio::spawn`, async channels `mpsc` |
| `15-backend-web-with-axum` | **Axum Web Framework** | Routing, State extractors, JSON response handlers, middleware |
| `16-database-access-with-sqlx` | **Database with SQLx** | Async connection pool, compile-time query verification |
| `17-cli-applications-file-io` | **CLI & File I/O** | `std::fs`, `BufReader`/`BufWriter`, command-line arguments |
| `18-multithreading-concurrency` | **Multithreading** | `std::thread`, message passing `mpsc`, shared state `Arc<Mutex<T>>` |
| `19-testing-benchmarking-tooling` | **Testing & Quality** | `#[test]`, `#[should_panic]`, integration tests, `cargo clippy` |
| `20-unsafe-rust-and-ffi` | **Unsafe & FFI** | Raw pointers (`*const T`, `*mut T`), `unsafe` blocks, C FFI binding |
| `21-interview-questions-and-drills` | **Interview Master Drill** | Top 10 high-yield Rust questions with runnable explanations |

---

## 🛠️ Run Any Module
```bash
cd 00-setup-and-cargo-toolchain
cargo run
# or
rustc main.rs && ./main
```

# 00 - Rust Setup & Installation Guide 🛠️

## 1. What is Rust?
Rust is a modern systems programming language focusing on safety, speed, and concurrency without requiring a garbage collector.

---

## 2. Installing Rust via `rustup` (Official)

### 🪟 Windows
1. Download `rustup-init.exe` from [https://rustup.rs/](https://rustup.rs/).
2. Requires Microsoft C++ Build Tools (Visual Studio).

### 🍎 macOS & 🐧 Linux
Run in terminal:
```bash
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
source $HOME/.cargo/env
```

---

## 3. Essential Toolchain Commands
```bash
rustc --version
cargo --version
rustup update
rustup component add clippy rustfmt
```

# 01 - Basics & Variables

- In Rust, variables are **immutable by default**.
- `const` requires explicit type annotation and is evaluated at compile time.
- **Shadowing** with `let` allows redeclaring a variable in the same scope.

children.name: main.rs
README.md

# 02 - Data Types & Memory

- `char` is **4 bytes** representing a full Unicode scalar value.
- Arrays `[T; N]` are allocated directly on the **stack**.

children.name: main.rs
README.md
children.content:
# 03 - Strings & Slices

- `String`: Owned heap buffer `(ptr, len, cap)` on stack.
- `&str`: Borrowed view `(ptr, len)` into UTF-8 data.

children.name: main.rs
README.md
children.content:
# 04 - Control Flow & Pattern Matching

- In Rust, `if` is an expression.
- `match` branches must be exhaustive.

children.name: main.rs
README.md
children.content:
# 05 - Functions & Closures

- `Fn`: Borrows captured variables immutably.
- `FnMut`: Borrows captured variables mutably.
- `FnOnce`: Takes ownership of captured variables.

children.name: main.rs

# 06 - Ownership, Borrowing & Lifetimes

### The Golden Rule of Borrowing:
At any given time, you can have **either** one mutable reference `&mut T` **OR** any number of immutable references `&T`, but not both.

- `impl Trait`: Static dispatch via monomorphization (zero runtime overhead).
- `dyn Trait`: Dynamic dispatch via vtable fat pointers.

# 10 - Error Handling

- `Option<T>` for nullable values (`Some(T)` or `None`).
- `Result<T, E>` for recoverable errors (`Ok(T)` or `Err(E)`).
- `?` operator unwraps `Ok` or returns early on `Err`.

# 11 - Smart Pointers & Interior Mutability

- `Box<T>`: Single owner on heap.
- `Rc<T>` / `Arc<T>`: Reference counted multiple ownership (single-threaded / multithreaded).
- `RefCell<T>` / `Mutex<T>`: Interior mutability with runtime borrow checks.
